turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen rolled her eyes at her mother’s questioning, telling Jack rather pointedly that she did not need a home in Belgrave Square to be happy.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack shifted nervously in his chair, telling Lady Bracknell that he did not wish to seem disrespectful but he felt that happiness was more important than a home in Belgrave Square.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell raised an eyebrow at Gwendolen’s comment, telling Jack that while happiness is indeed a desirable quality, it is not a sufficient foundation for marriage. She then looked pointedly at Gwendolen, reminding her daughter of the importance of considering practicalities.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack nodded in agreement, telling Lady Bracknell that he fully understood the importance of practical considerations but felt that personal happiness and affection were also crucial.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: She dismissed Jack’s sentiment with a wave of her hand, telling him that while affection is delightful in its place, it is the duty of a gentleman to provide stability and security for his wife. She then turned to Gwendolen, reminding her of the necessity of considering a suitor’s practical virtues.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen rolled her eyes, telling her mother that she would not be swayed by practical considerations when matters of the heart were involved.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: She dismissed Gwendolen’s sentiment with a sharp glance, telling her daughter that such romantic notions would not do in the real world and that a marriage must be based on solid foundations.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen was not swayed, telling her mother that true love would not be diminished by the practicalities of life.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack felt a bit uncomfortable, he told Lady Bracknell that he could understand her concerns and promised to be a reliable husband, but he hoped that Gwendolen would be allowed to consider her own feelings too.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: She dismissed Jack’s sentiment with a curt nod, telling him that while sincerity was commendable, it was paramount that a gentleman provide his wife with the means to lead a life of comfort and respectability, not just sentiment.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack felt somewhat awkward, he told Lady Bracknell that he fully agreed and reassured her that he would do everything in his power to ensure that Gwendolen would lead a comfortable and respectable life.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: She then enquired about Jack’s background and financial situation, telling him that while personal qualities were important, a gentleman must also be able to provide for his wife and uphold the family’s social standing.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack felt the pressure of Lady Bracknell's scrutiny, he told her that he was from a respectable background and that he would ensure his financial status met her expectations, adding that he hoped this would be enough for her to consider his suitability as a husband for Gwendolen.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: She raised an eyebrow, telling Jack that while his assurances were appreciated, she needed concrete evidence of his financial stability before she could consider him a suitable match for Gwendolen.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen rolled her eyes at her mother’s strict scrutiny, telling Lady Bracknell that Jack was a gentleman and more than capable of providing for her.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: She fixed her gaze upon Jack, telling him that while his assurances were commendable, she required proof of his financial stability and social standing before she could consider him a suitable match for Gwendolen.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack felt his palms getting sweaty, telling Lady Bracknell that he would provide her with the necessary documents and references to prove his financial stability and respectable background.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen was fed up with her mother’s scrutiny, she told Lady Bracknell that Jack was a gentleman of honour and that she would marry him regardless of her mother’s approval.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: She raised her chin slightly and informed Jack that while her daughter's enthusiasm was commendable, it was her duty to ensure that her future son-in-law possessed both a substantial income and impeccable credentials.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack felt a knot in his stomach, he told Lady Bracknell that he understood her concerns and would do everything in his power to prove himself worthy of Gwendolen.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Gwendolen told Lady Bracknell that she was engaged to Mr. Worthing, mamma.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen that she was not engaged to anyone and that when she did become engaged, she or her father would inform her of the fact.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Gwendolen told Lady Bracknell, 'Mamma!'

opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen to go to the carriage.

opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen to get into the carriage.

opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack to take a seat.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he preferred standing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she felt bound to inform him that he was not down on her list of eligible young men.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he must admit he smoked.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she was glad to hear it and that a man should always have an occupation of some kind.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he was twenty-nine.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell asked Jack if he knew everything or nothing.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he knew nothing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she was pleased to hear it and that she did not approve of anything that tampers with natural ignorance.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that his income was between seven and eight thousand a year.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell asked Jack if his income was in land or in investments.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that his income was in investments.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that it was satisfactory.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he had a country house with some land attached to it, about fifteen hundred acres.

opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that a country house was satisfactory and asked how many bedrooms it had.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he owned a house in Belgrave Square, but it was let by the year to Lady Bloxham.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she did not know Lady Bloxham.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that Lady Bloxham went about very little and was a lady considerably advanced in years.

opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that nowadays that was no guarantee of respectability of character and asked what number in Belgrave Square.
